previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileosigmoid anastomosis, was admitted with a one-week history of worsening right-sided abdominal pain, increased watery bowel movements up to 100 per day, and bright red blood per rectum. He had recently started Tysabri therapy. CT imaging showed worsening wall thickening and hyperemia in the sigmoid colon, consistent with active inflammatory bowel disease, with no evidence of obstruction or infection. Stool studies and CMV testing were negative. He was initially treated with antibiotics, which were discontinued after negative cultures. Due to persistent symptoms, a steroid burst with prednisone was initiated in consultation with his specialist, leading to improvement in bowel frequency and pain. His back pain was evaluated with MRI, which showed stable degenerative disc disease without new neurological compromise; he was managed with Percocet and tizanidine. He improved clinically, was transitioned to oral medications, and discharged home on a prednisone taper, continued Tysabri and B12 injections, and pain regimen with follow-up planned with GI and spine services.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old man with history of very frequent 
admissions for ___ disease (on Tysabri with last dose on 
___ and steroid taper from 50 mg at end of ___ to 5 mg 
now) and remote nephrolithiasis who presented with severe, 
colicky right sided flank pain. He had history of subtotal 
colectomy with ileosigmoid anastomosis with previous CT showing 
inflammation in that area (anastomosis) with stranding. This 
time he claimed unusal pain on the right side as he always had 
pain on the left side. He underwent a repeat CT scan of the 
abdomen and pelvis to rule out nephrolithiasis and further 
evaluate the thickening/inflammation seen on his last CT scan 
(which was in turn worse than on the prior scan). The admission 
CT showed no stones and worsening inflammation in that area. 
However, his right sided pain did not correlate with his CT 
findings and he had no fever or leukocytosis. He also described 
significant improvement of his chronic diarrhea prior to this 
admission. Most importantly his sed rate was normal. He also had 
no evidence of bowel obstruction and his KUB was without signs 
of small bowel obstruction. His U/A was clean without hematuria 
even though he claimed a streak of blood. He was treated 
initially with antibiotics (ampicillin-sulbactam). GI was 
consulted and narcotics were limited because of history of 
narcotic addiction (was on Methadone previously), frequent 
admissions, and suspicion of seeking behavior.

___ ultimately felt his did have active ___ at the area of 
his anastamosis.  He was started on IV solumedrol, and 
hydrocortisone enemas.  His pain was controlled with IV then PO 
opiates.  His tizanidine was increased while in house.

For further work up of his multifocal pain, CTU and GU 
ultrasound was performed which was normal.  MRI L spine was 
performed and showed no new acute issues consistent with exam to 
explain his pain.

Leg swelling: XRay of the ankle and LENIs were performed and 
showed no acute abnormlities.

He is discharged home on Prednisone 40mg which will be tapered 
by Dr ___ in outpatient setting, 10day of steroid enemas.  
His leukocytosis coincides with Steroid treatment.  He remained 
afebrile.

HISTORY:  ___ male with Crohn's and abdominal pain.

FINDINGS:  The cardiomediastinal and hilar contours are normal.  The lungs are
clear.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  The osseous structures
are intact.  There is no subdiaphragmatic free air.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process and no subdiaphragmatic free

MEDICAL HISTORY:  ___ man with Crohn's disease and nephrolithiasis
presenting with colicky right flank pain.  To evaluate for nephrolithiasis or
flareup in Crohn's.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen  dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT were acquired in axial images involving the
abdomen and the pelvis before and after administration of 130 mL of Optiray
contrast.  Oral contrast was also administered for the study.  Coronal and
sagittal reformats were performed at 5-mm slice thickness.

FINDINGS:  

Few, focal scattered areas of illdefined subpleural infiltrates are visualized
in bilateral lung bases.  No evidence of pericardial or pleural effusion
noted.

The liver, spleen, pancreas, bilateral adrenals and kidneys show normal CT
anatomy without any focal or diffuse lesions.  Normal pattern of enhancement
is also noted in the viscera.  The stomach is normal in caliber.

The patient is noted to be status post colonic resection with ileosigmoid
anastomosis.  In comparison to the previous study, the area of ileosigmoid
anastomosis and length of colonic resection could not be precisely localised
on this study. Please refer surgical notes for the same. A segment of bowel
loop at the expected rectosigmoid junction demonstrates thickened, enhancing
wall measuring about 6 cm atleast in length(4A;71. A prominent nodular
thickening is seen on the medial wall of this loop which may represent a
inflammatory intramural phlegmon.  There is  stranding of fat around the
abnormal-appearing loop noted.  The immediate small bowel loops proximal to
this segment appears to be mildly dilated. A few enhancing periaortic lymph
nodes are noted with no significant mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

There is no free air within the abdomen noted.

The bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles and ureters appear normal.  No
evidence of renal or ureteral calculi noted.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no acute fractures, dislocation, lytic or
sclerotic lesions suspicious for abnormality is noted.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of nephrolithiasis or ureteric calculi bilaterally.
2.  Status post colectomy with ileosigmoid anastomosis.  Inflammation
involving a bowel segment at the recto-sigmoid junction with a focal
intramural phlegmon is noted which demonstrates interval progression. Mildly
dilated bowel immediately proximal to this abnormal appearing segment is seen.
However, there is no evidence of free fluid,abscess, fistula or  free air
seen.

INDICATION:  History of nephrolithiasis, severe flank pain, assess for
hydronephrosis, obstruction or passing stone.

TECHNIQUE:  Renal ultrasound.

COMPARISONS:  CTU ___.

FINDINGS:  Right kidney measures 10.3 cm.  The left kidney measures 10.8 cm. 
There are two echogenic foci within the right kidney without definite
shadowing but with ringing down, which are likely vascular in nature.  There
is no definite evidence for stone, hydronephrosis, or mass.  The bladder is
normal in appearance.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence for stones, hydronephrosis, or mass.

INDICATION:  ___ man with Crohn's disease and history of

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1- and T2-weighted images of the lumbar spine were

FINDINGS:  Vertebral body height and alignment are normal.  Bone marrow signal

At T11-12, there is a disc bulge minimally indenting the ventral thecal sac,

The conus medullaris is normal in signal intensity, terminating at T12-L1.

The L1-2 through the L3-4 levels are unremarkable.

At L4-5, there is a mild disc bulge and facet arthropathy, left worse than

At L5-S1, there is an asymmetric disc bulge, slightly larger on the left,
which causes mild right and moderate left neural foraminal narrowing,

No signal abnormalities are identified in the imaged retroperitoneal soft

IMPRESSION:  Unchanged mild degenerative disease.  Moderate left and mild
right neural foraminal narrowing at L5-S1.

Three views of the right ankle show moderate soft tissue swelling on the
